title: Compact-test Dolbeault and de Rham formal-adjoint presentation
statement: Let $n\geq0$ and let $M$ be a complex manifold without boundary modeled on $\mathbf C^n$, with its Borel measurable structure. Use $A^\bullet(M)$, $A^{p,q}(M)$, a smooth positive definite Hermitian metric $g$, its metric volume $\mu$, and its integral pairing from [def-sfb-hermitian-dolbeault-data]. A smooth complex-linear endomorphism $S$ is a formal adjoint of $D$ when $\langle D\alpha,\eta\rangle_{L^2}=\langle\alpha,S\eta\rangle_{L^2}$ for every compactly supported smooth $\alpha$ and every smooth $\eta$. Compact support means compact closure of the set of points at which at least one exterior-degree component is nonzero. A formal Dolbeault presentation consists of complex-linear endomorphisms $\bar\partial,\partial,d^*,\bar\partial^*$ of these actual smooth forms. The first two have bidegrees $(0,1)$ and $(1,0)$. Their sum $d$ has zero exterior-degree-zero component and, in every holomorphic chart, its component in degree $k+1$ is the ordinary coordinate exterior derivative of the input component in degree $k$. The maps $d^*$ and $\bar\partial^*$ satisfy the preceding compact-test characterization for $d$ and $\bar\partial$, respectively. This defines an operator presentation by canonical characterizations, with no assumed differential relations or Laplacian identity; it imposes neither compactness of $M$ nor global integrability of arbitrary smooth forms.
